column2: The "deactivate a sales rep" pop-up: how it closes
column3: On the Sales By Representative report, when someone turns off a sales rep who still has customers assigned to them, a warning pop-up appears (it asks you to type "YES" to confirm). The written description says this pop-up should also close if you press the "Esc" key on the keyboard. But the app has a general house rule that pop-ups do NOT close with the "Esc" key. So the two say different things, and we don't know which one the finished app should follow.
column4: For this "deactivate a sales rep" pop-up, should pressing the "Esc" key close it, or not?
column5:
A) Yes - pressing "Esc" should close the pop-up (matches the written description).
B) No - pressing "Esc" should NOT close it (matches the app's general house rule); use only the Cancel and X buttons.

column2: Each report uses a different permission to view it
column3: These reports do not all use the same "who is allowed to see this" setting. The Sales By Customer report has its OWN dedicated permission. The Parts Velocity report and the Inventory Value report both reuse the existing inventory-reports permission. The Sales By Representative report is opened by anyone who can already see the other performance reports. We want to make sure this mix is on purpose before we lock in our tests for who can and cannot open each report.
column4: Is it intended that each report is controlled this way (some have their own permission, some share an existing one), rather than all six using one single "Reports" permission?
column5:
A) Yes - this mix is intended; keep it as described.
B) No - it should work differently (please tell us how).
column6: B -- these should be gated by normal reports access

column2: Are there any pictures or videos to check the reports against?

column4: Are there any design pictures, mock-ups, or videos for these reports that we should test the screens against - including the "companion video" mentioned for the Technician Utilization and Inventory Value reports?
column5:
